prompt.context_jp: 天天コーポレーションの朝___、コピー機の唸りと湯沸かしの音とともに始まる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 天天コーポレーションの朝___、コピー機の唸りと湯沸かしの音とともに始まる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the opening scene-setting description?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is setting up a general topic — 'as for the mornings at TenTen' — so は marks it as the frame for the description that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 'the morning' as new information, which doesn't fit a scene-setting opener. を is a direct object marker and doesn't work here.

prompt.context_jp: 健康診断で引っ掛かっちゃって、大腸___
prompt.prompt_jp: 健康診断で引っ掛かっちゃって、大腸___
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits as the mother reveals the issue?

feedback.correct_en: The mother is reporting newly discovered information — 'something came up with the large intestine'. が marks the new, previously unknown subject of concern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply '大腸' is an already-established topic being contrasted, which doesn't fit the shocked, first-time revelation.

contrast_examples.en: Apparently the large intestine is bad. (new info)
The large intestine is fine. (contrast/topic already established)

prompt.context_jp: 勝手ではないです。部長の承認___得ています。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部長の承認___得ています。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Hiramatsu's defense?

feedback.correct_en: Hiramatsu is contrastively emphasizing that at least the manager's approval has been obtained (even if the department hasn't discussed it). は highlights this as the key established fact.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark 'manager's approval' as new neutral information, missing the contrastive 'as for this part, I have it covered' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 窓花さん___、そもそも世話焼きなんです。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓花さん___、そもそも世話焼きなんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Madoka as the topic being described?

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is characterizing Madoka — 'as for Madoka, she's a natural caretaker'. は marks her as the topic that the rest of the sentence describes.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like identifying who the caretaker is among choices, not describing her nature.

prompt.context_jp: そんな空気の中、沙名子ひとり___、どちらの陣営にも与しない中庸の位置に立ち続けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子ひとり___、どちらの陣営にも与しない中庸の位置に立ち続けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle emphasizes Sanako alone standing apart?

feedback.correct_en: 'Sanako alone' is being singled out exhaustively — she is the one and only person maintaining neutrality. が marks this exclusive identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just mark her as a topic, losing the 'she alone, out of everyone' exclusivity that the narration emphasizes.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女だけが知っている。

prompt.context_jp: 結構 力___持ってるでしょ 経理部で。
prompt.prompt_jp: 結構 力___持ってるでしょ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'she holds power'?

feedback.correct_en: 持つ ('to hold/have') takes を to mark the thing possessed when used as an active verb — 'she holds power'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn 'power' into the subject, but 持ってる here is active possession by Moriwaka, requiring を.

prompt.context_jp: 友人の変化、母の不調、それら___同じ夜に重なることの意味を、彼女はうまく飲み込めずにいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: それら___同じ夜に重なることの意味を、彼女はうまく飲み込めずにいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside the embedded clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a noun-modifying clause (〜こと), the subject typically takes が, not は. 'The fact that they coincide' uses が to mark the subject of 重なる.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally doesn't appear inside relative/noun-modifying clauses as the subject marker.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来ることを知っている。
contrast_examples.en: I know that he's coming. (subordinate が)

prompt.context_jp: 母の名前___画面に浮かぶのを見て、彼女はわずかに眉をひそめる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母の名前___画面に浮かぶのを見て、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits as the mother's name appears on screen?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded 〜のを見る clause, the subject of 浮かぶ ('appear') is new perceived information — が marks it.
feedback.incorrect_en: は won't normally mark the subject inside a 〜の nominalized perception clause.

contrast_examples.en: I watched the rain fall. (subordinate が)

prompt.context_jp: 森若さんはどう思いますか？「私___…どちらでも」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___…どちらでも。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Sanako's noncommittal reply?

feedback.correct_en: Sanako is contrasting herself with others who have strong opinions — 'as for me, either is fine'. は marks the contrastive 'me (unlike you two)'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying 'it's me who...', which doesn't fit a hedged, personal stance.

contrast_examples.en: I'm fine either way. (as for me)

prompt.context_jp: うちの母ちゃん___田舎から送ってきたんですよ、トマト山ほど。
prompt.prompt_jp: うちの母ちゃん___田舎から送ってきたんですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Yamada explaining who sent the tomatoes?

feedback.correct_en: Yamada is introducing 'my mom' as new information — the agent who sent them. が marks this newly-introduced subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame mom as an already-known topic, but Yamada is bringing her up for the first time to explain the tomatoes.

prompt.context_jp: 「トマト___医者いらず」って言いますけど…
prompt.prompt_jp: 「トマト___医者いらず」って言いますけど…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the proverb?

feedback.correct_en: Generic proverbs stating a general truth about a topic use は — 'as for tomatoes, (they are) doctor-free'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying which thing is 'doctor-free', not stating a general truth.

prompt.context_jp: うちの社員___公務員じゃないんだし。
prompt.prompt_jp: うちの社員___公務員じゃないんだし。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the Shinbatta's explanation?

feedback.correct_en: Shinbatta is characterizing 'our employees' as a topic — 'as for our employees, they aren't civil servants'. は fits identifying attributes/categorization.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify who is not a civil servant among options, which isn't the point.

prompt.context_jp: 人に借りを作るほど怖いこと___ないわ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 人に借りを作るほど怖いこと___ないわ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in 'nothing is scarier than...'?

feedback.correct_en: The 〜ほど…はない construction ('nothing is as X as Y') idiomatically takes は for the negated superlative.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't fit the fixed 'ほど〜はない' pattern; the construction requires は to express 'there is nothing (that compares)'.

contrast_examples.jp: これほど美味しいものはない。
contrast_examples.en: Nothing is as delicious as this. (fixed pattern)

prompt.context_jp: こうして誰かがいれてくれたコーヒー___一番うまいよ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰かがいれてくれたコーヒー___一番うまいよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Yoshimura's 'this is the best coffee' declaration?

feedback.correct_en: '一番〜' (superlative) typically takes が to exclusively identify 'this one, out of all, is the best'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just topicalize it without the exclusive 'this is THE best' identification nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 平松の指先が、書類___沙名子の前にきちんと差し出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 書類___沙名子の前にきちんと差し出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the documents?

feedback.correct_en: 差し出す ('present/hold out') is a transitive verb — the documents are its direct object, marked by を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the documents the subject (impossible — fingertips do the action). に marks destination, not object.

prompt.context_jp: バス停の隅で、聞き覚えのある声___鋭く耳に飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 聞き覚えのある声___鋭く耳に飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the narrative introduction of the voice?

feedback.correct_en: A new, suddenly perceived element entering the scene — 'a familiar voice' — gets が as new-information marking.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would present the voice as already-known topic, but the narration is describing a fresh perceptual event.

contrast_examples.en: The sound is quiet. (describing known topic)

prompt.context_jp: いいえ、有給取得は社員の権利なので、休んで___だけです。
prompt.prompt_jp: 有給取得は社員の権利なので、休んで___だけです。
prompt.prompt_en: What verb form fits Hiramatsu's slightly stiff reply?

feedback.correct_en: 休んでいた ('was taking time off') is the plain descriptive continuous — Hiramatsu is matter-of-factly stating what she did on her right to leave.
feedback.incorrect_en: あげた implies doing a favor for someone else; もらった implies receiving a favor. Neither fits exercising one's own entitlement.

contrast_examples.jp: 休ませてもらいました。

prompt.context_jp: ホントに___なあ、窓花ちゃんは。
prompt.prompt_jp: ホントに___なあ、窓花ちゃんは。
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression fits Kamamoto praising Madoka?

feedback.correct_en: 気が利く means 'thoughtful/attentive' — exactly what Kamamoto is complimenting Madoka for anticipating his coffee craving.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気が重い means 'feel heavy/reluctant'; 気が済む means 'be satisfied'. Neither fits a compliment.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子は映画のチケットを受け取りながら内心でつぶやく:「___より怖いものはない」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___より怖いものはない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the proverb?

feedback.correct_en: タダより怖いものはない ('nothing is scarier than something free') is a well-known idiom — free gifts come with hidden obligations.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other words don't form the fixed proverb; the idiom specifically warns against 'free' things.

contrast_examples.jp: タダより高いものはない。
contrast_examples.en: Nothing is more expensive than free. (variant)

prompt.context_jp: 賄賂を受け取る代わりにお金を貸してもらってるってことですよね？___じゃないですか！
prompt.prompt_jp: ___じゃないですか、一大事ですよ！
prompt.prompt_en: What legal term fits Sasaki's outburst?

feedback.correct_en: 贈収賄 (bribery) fits Sasaki's reading of the situation — exchanging money for favorable business decisions. Shinbatta later corrects this to 背任行為.
feedback.incorrect_en: 背任行為 is Shinbatta's more precise correction (since they aren't civil servants). 横領 (embezzlement) involves misappropriating entrusted assets, not this scenario.

prompt.context_jp: 自分が輝ける居場所は自分で作らなきゃダメよ。「___先は闇」って言葉もあるじゃない？
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom used by Hiramatsu.

feedback.correct_en: 一寸先は闇 ('one inch ahead is darkness') is a fixed proverb meaning the future is unknown/unpredictable.
feedback.incorrect_en: The idiom specifically uses 一寸 (a very short unit of distance). The other options don't form the established proverb.

prompt.context_jp: そんなに人の___取んのが楽しいですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: そんなに人の___取んのが楽しいですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Complete Yoshimura's retort to Shinbatta.

feedback.correct_en: 揚げ足を取る is an idiom meaning 'to nitpick / catch someone on a slip of the tongue' — exactly what Yoshimura accuses Shinbatta of.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other words don't form this idiom; 揚げ足 (lifted foot, from sumo/judo) is the fixed element.

contrast_examples.en: To take advantage of someone's weakness.

prompt.context_jp: そう、自分の未来に___をまくためのね。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の未来に___をまくためのね。
prompt.prompt_en: What word fits Hiramatsu's metaphor about investment?

feedback.correct_en: 種をまく ('to sow seeds') is a fixed collocation meaning to plant seeds (literal or metaphorical for future results).
feedback.incorrect_en: 花 (flower) and 芽 (sprout) don't collocate with まく; you sow 種, which later becomes 芽 and then 花.

prompt.context_jp: Hiramatsu greeting the department head after summer leave.
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting sounds most natural for returning to work after vacation?

choices.text: 部長、今日から戻りました。
部長、今日から戻ります。
部長、今日から帰りました。

feedback.correct_en: 戻りました (past tense of 戻る, 'to return (to one's post)') naturally announces 'I'm back as of today'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 戻ります (future/non-past) sounds like a future declaration, not an announcement of arrival. 帰る means to go home, so 帰りました would mean 'I went home' — the wrong direction.

prompt.context_jp: Sanako responding to Yamada's informal offer at her accounting desk.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing best matches Sanako's formal, workplace tone?

choices.text: 領収書でしたら、休憩後にお願いします。
領収書だったら、休憩のあとで。
領収書なら、あとでいいよ。

feedback.correct_en: 〜でしたら and お願いします maintain Sanako's characteristically polite, measured business tone with colleagues.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual-conversational; C is overtly informal with よ, both out of character for Sanako at her accounting counter.

contrast_examples.jp: ご質問でしたら後ほど。
contrast_examples.en: If you have questions, later please. (polite)

prompt.context_jp: Hiramatsu on the phone pleading for a payment extension.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for apologetically asking someone to wait?

choices.text: ちょっと待っていただけると助かります。
ちょっと待ってもらうと助かります。
ちょっと待ってくれると助かります。

feedback.correct_en: いただけると is the humble/polite form appropriate when asking a business creditor for a favor — it matches Hiramatsu's deferential posture.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらう is neutral; くれる is familiar. Neither matches the pleading-with-a-business-partner register that Hiramatsu uses.

contrast_examples.jp: お待ちいただけますか。

prompt.context_jp: Sanako politely ending the awkward hallway encounter with Yamada.
prompt.prompt_en: Which closing phrase best fits Sanako's reserved, polite style?

choices.text: お気遣いありがとうございます。失礼します。
気を遣ってくれてありがとう。じゃあね。
気にしてくれてサンキュー。バイバイ。

feedback.correct_en: お気遣い (humble noun) + 失礼します is the measured, polite exit Sanako habitually uses — maintaining distance even in an emotional moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is friendly-casual, C is overly informal — both clash with Sanako's cool, boundaries-maintained persona.
